title: Machine Learning for Human Factors Analysis in Railway Safety Reports
course: CSCI 6379, Dr. Dongchul Kim, The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
summary: We are classifying six kinds of events in NASA’s railway close-call reports, using coded fields about people, conditions and operations, plus the reporters’ own words.

done.title: Literature review
done.detail: Seven studies on railway safety reports and close calls.

done.title: Dataset obtained
done.detail: All NASA C3RS close-call reports from the CRAFT export.

done.title: Data exploration
done.detail: Fields profiled, targets chosen, data quality checked.

done.title: Data cleaned and prepared
done.detail: Coded fields converted to model inputs, odd values fixed, and reports split into training (70%), validation (15%) and test (15%) sets.

done.title: RQ1: Model comparison on coded fields
done.detail: Logistic Regression, Random Forest and XGBoost trained and scored on all six event types.

next.title: RQ2: Does report text help?
next.detail: Add the narrative, synopsis and follow-up interviews as text features and compare.

next.title: RQ3: Which factors matter most
next.detail: Measure how much each field and group of fields contributes.

next.title: Neural network on all six event types
next.detail: Extend our neural network from one event type to six.

neural_network.description: Our neural network’s validation score on its first run, predicting Station Operations only.

research_questions.question: To what extent can structured human-factor, environmental, personnel, and operational features classify the six recorded event categories?
Does adding report summaries, narratives, or callbacks improve event-category classification compared with structured features alone?
Which structured features are most informative for classifying the six recorded event categories?
